For a challenge, v/collaborate's first project is a circular reference. D'oh!

If you have experience in CSS, graphic design, moderation, or project management, then we're interested in your input regarding ways to improve v/collaborate. Actually...even if you don't have experience in any of those areas, we're still interested in anything you might have to contribute regarding the layout, operation, creative direction, or applications of this subverse. We're also looking for eager and active users to become our first moderation team.

Voat is new, and this community is even newer; unlike many subverses, we aren't seeking to clone an existing board (or "sub") from another site. I'm also not interested in creating a walled garden run by a handful of opinionated or closed-minded moderators, and my expertise in project-related fields is (of course) limited to a tiny fraction of the whole. Thus, in the (newly minted) spirit of v/collaborate, I'm putting just about every detail of this subverse up for discussion and review, by any eager members of the growing community. Think my ideas are terrible? Well, they often are -- and I want to hear your alternatives.

Here's a few of my own thoughts to get the ball rolling (but please don't hesitate to go elsewhere with the discussion):

  • Flair/Tags/Sorting: it seems reasonable to me that a project- and team-based board should allow tagging of posts to differentiate proposals, offers, introductions, resources, and other types of posts in a filter-capable way. However, I'm not sure what structure this system should take, nor of the details. Should flair (or tags) be required on every post? Should users be allowed to self-tag their interests, skills, availability, etc; should this be subject to moderator verification and approval?
  • Protocol: Should we aim for a consistent standard protocol in handling ideas, intros, projects, requests, (etc) and for managing communication (by thread, by message, etc), or allow each user to work with their own preferences?
  • Service Integration: as a tech engineer, I am partial to Slack, Asana, and a number of other existing services for project management and team communication. Should we seek to integrate v/collaboration with these (or other) services?
  • Wiki: it seems obvious a subverse like this should have a central wiki (or other platform), covering standards and common knowledge. Any other applications?
  • Privacy: members interested in working on private, sensitive, or commerically-viable projects would obviously require a team channel apart from the public board at large. Voat's direct-messaging capabilities aren't bad, but lack some of the required capabilities (multi-user chat, boards/replies, etc). Many would also prefer a system which cannot be read/accessed by site administrators, or accidentally shared/publicized.
  • Legal: serious projects may benefit from a community TOS or other enforceable policy regarding legal matters, such as accountability, ownership, contractual establishment, etc. Shared resources (like a stock NDA template) lower the entry barrier for cautious voaters' private and commercial projects. Alternately, a simple (wiki?) FAQ or advice post for prudent setup and management may be sufficient. It's also my opinion that v/collaborate itself should have some defense against liability claims. Of course, IANAL (but you might be!)
  • Multiverse: I believe v/collaborate could only benefit from a strong working relationship with other technical, DIY, and project-related communities, on Voat and elsewhere. At minimum, sidebar cross-linking would assist users seeking help, advice, or contacts in a specific field (for example, programming). Other subverses similar to ours like CrazyIdeas, DIY, and GetEducated most welcome. Any active users/moderators of these communities, please feel free to reach out directly and we'll add you to our sidebar.

As always, thanks for collaborating!
